chunks: And Ibn Isma'il narrated from Fadalah from Ibn Abi Ya'fur who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Dhihar from his slave girl, so he said: 'It is like the Dhihar of a free woman.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: To perform Dhihar, a specific form of verbal divorce in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Dhihar for a slave girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the legal consequences of *Dhihar* (verbal divorce) against a slave girl are identical to those against a free woman, specifically regarding the expiation (*Kaffarah*) and waiting period. This ruling underscores the principle of legal parity between slave and free women in marital jurisprudence, a key point of discussion among Shia jurists regarding the extent of rights retained by concubines. The hadith reinforces the application of general marital rules to specific cases of concubinage, ensuring consistency in the treatment of women regardless of their social status.
